learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify manufacturing processes according to their basic functionality, corresponding to the six main groups (DIN 8580).
Students are able to specify the essential manufacturing processes of the six main groups (DIN 8580) and explain their functions.

Students are able to describe the characteristic process features (geometry, materials, accuracy, tools, machines) of the essential manufacturing processes of the six main groups according to DIN 8580.
Students are able to derive the relevant process-specific technical advantages and disadvantages from the characteristic process features.
Students are able to select suitable manufacturing processes for given components.
Students are able to integrate the manufacturing processes required for the production of given example products into a process chain.

syllabus_topics: Urformen (Casting, Plastics Technology, Sintering, Additive Manufacturing Processes)
Forming (Sheet Metal Forming, Bulk Metal Forming)
Separating (Machining with geometrically defined and undefined cutting edge, Cutting, Ablation)
